te: Preparing the Uthai Thani site visit on 12–13 November and continuing the draft report
se: The meeting prepared the study visit to the Bangkok stray dog shelter in Thap Than District, Uthai Thani Province, to hear about how stray animals are managed and to see a mobile sterilisation unit, and continued considering the draft study report
it: Preparations for the study visit, Uthai Thani Province
The subcommittee's draft study report

te: Meeting summary video · Preparing the Uthai Thani site visit on 12–13 November and continuing the draft report
Summary of the visit to the Prawet dog control centre, and preparations for the Uthai Thani visit
se: The meeting considered the schedule of the study visit to the Bangkok stray dog shelter in Thap Than District, Uthai Thani Province, summarised the visit to the Bangkok dog control centre in Prawet District on 7 October 2026, and considered the subcommittee's draft study report
it: Study visit schedule: Bangkok stray dog shelter, Thap Than District, Uthai Thani Province
Summary of the study visit to the Bangkok dog control centre, Prawet District, 7 October 2026
The subcommittee's draft study report

te: Meeting summary video · Summary of the visit to the Prawet dog control centre, and preparations for the Uthai Thani visit
Consideration begins of the draft report on "Managing Stray Dogs for the Systematic Prevention and Solution of Rabies"
se: The meeting considered the draft study report on "Managing Stray Dogs for the Systematic Prevention and Solution of Rabies" and the schedule of the study visit to the dog control centre in Prawet District, Bangkok
it: Draft study report on managing stray dogs for the systematic prevention and solution of rabies
Study visit schedule: dog control centre, Prawet District, Bangkok

te: Role of the provincial administration during outbreaks noted, and a visit to a dog control centre planned
se: The meeting noted information from the Department of Provincial Administration that in normal times district chiefs inform the public through kamnan, village heads, village health volunteers and volunteers, and that during an outbreak they coordinate with public health officials and report to the provincial governor. It also discussed study visits to 2 places: the Bangkok dog control centre in Prawet District in early October, and the Bangkok stray dog shelter in Thap Than District, Uthai Thani Province, in November
it: The role of the provincial administration in preventing the spread of communicable diseases
Draft schedule for study visits on stray animal management, Bangkok and Uthai Thani Province

te: The Department of Local Administration gives information on the Thailand Rabies Awards model local authority project
se: The meeting invited a representative of the Department of Local Administration to give information on the model local authority project for rabies prevention and control (Thailand Rabies Awards), including its assessment criteria, cooperation between agencies and budget, so that it can be extended nationwide
it: Model local authority project for rabies prevention and control

te: The Department of Provincial Administration explains its role in rabies control
se: After deaths rose steadily over 3 years, from 5 to 7 and 10, a representative of the Department of Provincial Administration explained that shelters, sterilisation and animal care are the responsibility of local authorities, and that the provincial administration is ready to help through monthly meetings of kamnan and village heads in 878 districts. The meeting proposed training kamnan, village heads and village health volunteers, and prepared to invite the Department of Local Administration to the next meeting
it: The role of the provincial administration in rabies prevention and control

te: Phuket and Sukhothai cited as models of rabies-free areas; the Department of Provincial Administration to be invited
se: The meeting discussed the stray dog situation, which is still a challenge in many areas, citing Phuket and Sukhothai Provinces, which have been declared rabies-free areas, as case studies. It felt that the Director-General of the Department of Provincial Administration should be invited to discuss the role of local bodies in registration, sterilisation, vaccination and budgets
it: Approaches to stray dogs and rabies control

te: 3 veterinary professional bodies give information on rabies control
se: The meeting invited the President of the Veterinary Council of Thailand, the President of the Small Animal Veterinary Practitioners Association of Thailand and the President of the Thai Veterinary Medical Association under the Royal Patronage to give information on disease control measures in animal hospitals, registration and raising awareness among people who work with animals, for the study in 4 dimensions: dog population management, vaccination, disease surveillance and the law
it: Rabies control measures and the stray dog problem

te: The Department of Disease Control and the Department of Health explain: most deaths came from owned animals that were not vaccinated
se: The Department of Disease Control reported 10 rabies deaths so far this year, more than last year, mostly from pets that have owners but were not vaccinated. The Department of Health said that only about 30 per cent of local authorities have issued local ordinances to control pets. The subcommittee proposed 5 measures, such as urging local authorities to issue ordinances, setting up observation and quarantine centres, providing pre-exposure vaccination for front-line officials, teaching through schools, and integrating databases
it: The rabies situation
5 proposed measures to prevent and control rabies

te: Discussion with the National Statistical Office: one national standard for dog and cat data
se: The meeting discussed with the National Statistical Office how to collect data on dog and cat populations, especially stray animals, which are not yet in the agricultural census and are hard to count. The Office felt that in the short term, statistical estimates could be made from existing data. The subcommittee proposed that the Office act as the central agency setting data standards and definitions, so that all agencies use the same reference figures
it: Collecting and developing a database of dog and cat populations

te: Follow-up on the Rabies One Data dog and cat population database
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Department of Local Administration and the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Kasetsart University, to give information on Rabies One Data, the central database of dog and cat populations. Surveys are made 2 times a year by local authorities, and the provincial local administration offices check the data before it is used at national level
it: The Rabies One Data dog and cat population database

te: Results of the Department of Livestock Development's oral rabies vaccine trials noted
se: The meeting considered approaches to managing stray dogs and controlling rabies, and noted information on the oral rabies vaccine (ORV) that the Department of Livestock Development is researching for dogs that are hard to catch. Field trials found that dogs readily ate the bait and developed immunity close to that of the injected vaccine, but storage and the handling of leftover bait still need attention
it: Oral rabies vaccine (ORV)

te: Who is responsible when a dog injures a person: clearly separate owned from ownerless dogs
se: The meeting discussed approaches to the stray dog problem, including law enforcement, owners' responsibilities and the vaccination system. It felt that when a dog injures a person, it should be made clear whether the animal has an owner. If it has an owner, the owner is liable under the law; if it has none, the local authority acts as the law provides
it: Responsibility when dogs injure people, and law enforcement

te: A single stray dog database and an oral rabies vaccine proposed
se: The meeting followed up progress and set a strategy towards "a sustainably rabies-free Thailand". It proposed a single central database (One Database) shared by all agencies, and using the oral rabies vaccine for the first time in high-risk areas such as rubbish dumps and border areas. It noted Bangkok's "fried-egg pan" disease control model, and proposed one standard mark nationwide, such as clipping the right ear of sterilised animals
it: Central stray dog database (One Database)
Oral rabies vaccine and the CNVR approach
